origin_result.basis: No checks were performed because the following required information is missing: a bill of materials (each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency) and a declaration (product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, operations done in the UAE).

procedure.step: The factory must be registered through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service before applying for a certificate of origin; registration requires a factory located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter applies for the certificate of origin through the Ministry of Foreign Trade's 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service by logging in, filling the form, uploading required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), paying the fee online, and submitting; processing takes about one working day.

The application must include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately; the issuing authority may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 10 to AED 200, depending on the invoice value in AED.

The certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from issue, covers only one import, and must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it can be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.

The exporter must ship directly from the UAE to India; if transit through another country is necessary, the goods must remain under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage. Third-party invoicing is allowed but must be indicated.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information including which origin criterion is claimed, and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing; the importer must answer customs requests within 10 working days.

The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue; refusal to consent to a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

caveats.note: The CEPA lowers the duty on this line but does not remove it.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
No usable shipment value (positive amount and currency), so only rates are given.
